# fasttrop

Estimate the effect of a policy or other treatment in panel data with
the Triply Robust Panel (TROP) estimator. The model fits run in C, so
the results come fast.

New here? [TROP in plain
words](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/the-big-idea.md) What
the method does and why its authors made it.

Ready to try it? [Get
started](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/fasttrop.md) Install
the package and make your first estimate.

Want the evidence? [How we checked
fasttrop](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/validation.md)
Agreement with other packages, tests, and simulations.

## What fasttrop does

Some units get a treatment, for example a new law, and other units do
not. fasttrop estimates how the treatment changed an outcome of the
treated units. For each treated unit and period, it calculates the
outcome without the treatment from the untreated data. Three ideas
control this calculation:

- Units with a similar history get more weight.
- Periods near the treated period get more weight.
- A model finds patterns that all units share over time.

The data select how much each idea counts. fasttrop then averages the
effects of all treated cells. This average is the average treatment
effect on the treated (ATT). The standard error and the confidence
interval show how uncertain the estimate is.

**Fast** In our benchmarks with one thread and fixed tuning parameters,
fasttrop was 25 to 174 times faster than the Python packages. Times
depend on the computer.

**Checked** On four test panels, the local ATTs of fasttrop and
`diff-diff` differed by at most 4e-8. The gap to the authors’ package is
up to 2.5e-5, the same as the gap between the two Python packages.

**Three designs** The local method can calculate results for block,
staggered, and general designs. The triple robustness proof is only for
a block design.

**Covariates** Both methods can use covariates, the term of Section 6.2
of the paper. Refer to the article [Use
covariates](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/covariates.md).

## Know the limits

- The triple robustness result has a proof only for a block design.
- The bootstrap interval is reliable only with many treated units.
  fasttrop gives a warning message below five treated units.
- The global method works only for a block design.
- With covariates, the weights do not remove a bias from a wrong
  covariate coefficient.
- In our simulations with larger trends for the treated units, TROP
  reduced the bias, but some bias stayed. In a staggered design, the
  bias was 20% smaller than the bias of TWFE imputation.
- Our simulations with a staggered design have 60 units, four cohorts,
  and one tuning grid. We did not compare TROP with other modern
  estimators on real data.
- fasttrop follows arXiv version 3 of the paper. A line-by-line check
  against the journal version is not complete.

The article [What TROP can and cannot
do](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/limits.md) explains each
limit.

## Install the package

fasttrop is not on CRAN at this time. To install the package from
GitHub, do these steps:

1.  Make sure that you have a C compiler. On Windows, Rtools has the
    compiler.
2.  If you do not have the `remotes` package, install it.
3.  Run this R code:

``` r

remotes::install_github("farach/fasttrop")
```

## A first example

``` r

library(fasttrop)

# A practice panel: 8 of 40 units get the treatment in the last 5 periods.
panel <- trop_simulate(n_units = 40, n_periods = 20, n_treated = 8, n_post = 5,
                       seed = 1)

fit <- trop(panel, outcome = "y", treatment = "d", unit = "unit", time = "time",
            cv_cells = 200, n_boot = 200, seed = 1)
summary(fit)
```

The article [Get
started](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/fasttrop.md)
explains each step and the output.

## After your first fit

- To see how the effect changes after treatment starts, use [Effects by
  group and many
  tests](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/event-studies.md).
  The example shows how to read the band for all event times.
- For a study with start dates, many groups, and a long bootstrap, use
  [Plan, run, and examine a large
  study](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/large-studies.md).
  It shows how to count the cells before you see the results.
- If the fit reports a value at the edge of the grid, use [Choose a
  tuning
  grid](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/tuning-grid.md). It
  shows how to change the grid when you change the units of the outcome.

## Who made what

The TROP method is from Susan Athey, Guido Imbens, Zhaonan Qu, and
Davide Viviano (2026). fasttrop is an independent R package by Alex
Farach. The authors of the method did not write this package. If you use
fasttrop, cite the paper. The [citation
page](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/authors.html#citation) gives the
references.

# Package index

## Estimate effects

Calculate the TROP estimate for a data frame or for matrices.

- [`trop()`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop.md) :
  Triply Robust Panel (TROP) estimator
- [`trop_matrix()`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_matrix.md)
  : TROP estimator for outcome and treatment matrices

## Read the results

Show a fit and get its parts.

- [`print(`*`<trop>`*`)`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop-methods.md)
  [`summary(`*`<trop>`*`)`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop-methods.md)
  [`print(`*`<summary.trop>`*`)`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop-methods.md)
  [`coef(`*`<trop>`*`)`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop-methods.md)
  [`confint(`*`<trop>`*`)`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop-methods.md)
  [`vcov(`*`<trop>`*`)`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop-methods.md)
  [`as.data.frame(`*`<trop>`*`)`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop-methods.md)
  :

  Methods for `trop` objects

## Plan a study

Make the treatment and the target from start dates, and count the cells
of each group.

- [`trop_rollout()`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_rollout.md)
  : Make the treatment and the target from start dates
- [`trop_cells()`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_cells.md)
  [`print(`*`<trop_cells>`*`)`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_cells.md)
  : Count the cells of each group before the bootstrap

## Group effects and many tests

Get the effect of groups of cells, combine the effects, and adjust the
p-values of many tests.

- [`trop_effects()`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_effects.md)
  [`print(`*`<trop_effects>`*`)`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_effects.md)
  [`as.data.frame(`*`<trop_effects>`*`)`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_effects.md)
  [`coef(`*`<trop_effects>`*`)`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_effects.md)
  [`vcov(`*`<trop_effects>`*`)`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_effects.md)
  : Effects by event time, cohort, period, or unit
- [`trop_contrast()`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_contrast.md)
  : Linear combinations of group effects
- [`trop_stepdown()`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_stepdown.md)
  [`print(`*`<trop_stepdown>`*`)`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_stepdown.md)
  : Romano-Wolf stepdown p-values
- [`trop_boot_rows()`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_boot_rows.md)
  : Make bootstrap rows
- [`trop_honest_inputs()`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_honest_inputs.md)
  : Inputs for a sensitivity analysis of pre-trends

## Settings

Set the solver options, the tuning grids, and the number of threads.

- [`trop_control()`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_control.md)
  : Solver options
- [`trop_grid()`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_grid.md)
  : Tuning grids
- [`trop_grid_scaled()`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_grid_scaled.md)
  : Scale the tuning grid to the data
- [`trop_threads()`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_threads.md)
  : Default number of threads

## Practice data

Make a panel with a known effect.

- [`trop_simulate()`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_simulate.md)
  : Simulated panel with a factor structure

Learn the idea of TROP and make your first estimate.

  words](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/the-big-idea.md):

  What the Triply Robust Panel estimator does, why its authors made it,
  and what “triply robust” means.

- [Get started with
  fasttrop](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/fasttrop.md):

## Use fasttrop

Read the results of a fit and know the limits of the method.

- [How to read your
  results](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/read-your-results.md):

  What each number in the output of fasttrop means, and what to do when
  fasttrop gives a warning message.

- [Use
  covariates](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/covariates.md):

  How fasttrop adds covariates to TROP, the two procedures for the
  coefficients, and how we checked them.

- [Effects by group and many
  tests](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/event-studies.md):

  How to get the effect for each event time, how to keep some treated
  cells out of the estimate, and how to adjust p-values for many tests.

- [Plan, run, and examine a large
  study](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/large-studies.md):

  How to make the treatment, the target, and the event times from start
  dates, count the cells before you see the results, run a long
  bootstrap with a checkpoint, and read the diagnostics of the draws.

- [Choose a tuning
  grid](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/tuning-grid.md):

  Set the grid for the units of the outcome. Read a grid warning and
  decide which values to try next.

- [What TROP can and cannot
  do](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/limits.md):

  The limits of the method and of this package in plain words, and good
  practice for an analysis.

## The evidence

See how we checked the results and the speed of the package.

- [How we checked
  fasttrop](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/validation.md):

  The comparisons with other implementations, the tests of the tuning
  and the bootstrap, and the simulations with a known effect.

- [How fast is
  fasttrop?](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/speed.md):

  Why speed matters for TROP, what makes fasttrop fast, and how to make
  your own runs faster.
